content: 1. In the study by O'Farrell (2006) conducted in Lao PDR, the time series analysis revealed that Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) and Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) rates were lower. 2. In the research by Wi (2006) conducted in the Philippines, the time series data indicated that NG and CT rates were lower, while contraceptive use (CU) rates were higher. 3. McKormick (2007) conducted a time series study in Bangladesh, which demonstrated that NG and CT rates were lower, CU rates were also lower, and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels were reduced. 4. Bollen (2010) performed a time series analysis in Indonesia, showing that NG and CT rates were lower, while CU rates were higher. 5. Bruce (2011) conducted a time series study in Papua New Guinea, which found that NG and CT rates were lower, whereas CU rates were higher.
